evals.prompt: Using the best-practices skill, review this for supply-chain risk: <script src="https://cdn.example.com/lib@1.2.3/dist/lib.js"></script>, loaded from a CDN we don't control. What's missing?
evals.expected_output: Flags the missing Subresource Integrity (SRI) hash, explaining that without it a compromised CDN can serve modified/malicious code and the browser has no way to detect it, and recommends adding an integrity attribute plus crossorigin.

assertions.text: Recommends the integrity attribute with crossorigin

evals.prompt: Using the best-practices skill, review this code for security: element.innerHTML = userInput;. What's the risk and what should replace it?
evals.expected_output: Flags this as an XSS vulnerability since userInput could contain executable markup, and recommends using textContent for plain text or sanitizing with a library like DOMPurify if HTML is actually required.

assertions.text: Flags this as an XSS risk
Recommends textContent or a sanitizer as the fix

evals.prompt: Using the best-practices skill: our webpack config has devtool: 'source-map' unconditionally, including in the production build. Is this a problem, and what should change?
evals.expected_output: Flags that shipping full source maps in production exposes unminified original source code to anyone who requests the .map file, and recommends hidden-source-map (or no source maps) in production, uploading them privately to an error tracker instead.

assertions.text: Flags exposing source maps in production as a problem
Recommends hidden-source-map or disabling maps in production
